## Feasibility steps in GREG

1.  The feasibility of your UC proposal will already be explored before the UCPTF. From your study outline, WP6 will gather the relevant information for a first-step feasibility exploration to inform the UCPTF before proceeding with a UC. This first feasibility assessment, named **landscaping**, includes:

    - **Potential database information**: national/regional, primary care/secondary care, etc.

    - **Codelist with 40 concept ids**: an Excel file with \~40 *concept id*s that will be relevant for your study. Tools that will help you build this codelist are [Athena](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/start) and [ATLAS](https://atlas-demo.ohdsi.org/#/home), that will be better explained in the [ATLAS section](atlas.qmd).

2.  Once your study is already ongoing and you are finishing the study protocol, you will need to prepare for the final feasibility exploration report. You will need to define 5 different phenotypes for your study (see [Phenotyping section](phenotyping.qmd)). These 5 phenotypes will be run in the available databases, from the GREG consortium and the [EHDEN portal](https://portal.ehden.eu/). Counts for all different *concept id*s included in your phenotypes' concept sets, will be reported in an exploration report, along with attrition tables.

    - Once you have the exploration report with feasibility results, you can select up to 10 databases for your study.

      ::: callout-note
      Please, provide a rule or quantitative way (score) for deciding your final 10 databases. You will need to justify your choices.
      :::

::: callout-tip
You can always ask WP6 (Lucia C. and Lucia B.) to assist you with your choices or phenotype development!
:::
